title: Tuning Kubernetes HPA for Sudden Traffic Surges
prompt: A ticketing API runs on Kubernetes (minReplicas=10, maxReplicas=120) with a standard CPU HPA targeting 70% utilization. When a concert ticket drop hits at 10:00:00, RPS jumps 10x (from 2,000 to 20,000 RPS) in 12 seconds. Pods saturate CPU and drop connections within 20 seconds, yet HPA does not trigger scale-up until 10:01:15. New pods then sit in Pending for 110 seconds waiting for Karpenter/Cluster Autoscaler to provision EC2 nodes, plus 35 seconds for JVM warmup and readinessProbe. By the time capacity arrives at 10:03:40 (~3.7 minutes late), 45% of checkout requests have timed out with HTTP 503. Redesign the autoscaling and surge-absorption architecture to handle 10x spikes in < 30 seconds.

spark.summary: Default CPU-based HPA suffers a 3–5 minute blind spot during flash traffic surges due to metrics-server scrape intervals, HPA sync loops, container startup, and Cluster Autoscaler node provisioning.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, switch from lagging CPU utilization to leading request-rate/queue-depth metrics via KEDA/Prometheus Adapter, pre-warm capacity with over-provisioning pause pods, and protect pods during scale-up with readiness-aware load shedding.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A ticketing API (`minReplicas=10`, `maxReplicas=120`, `200 RPS/pod` at 70% CPU) jumps from `2,000` to `20,000 RPS` in `12 seconds` during a concert drop.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 145s CPU+EC2 Lag vs. <15s Leading Metric & Warm Buffer (20k RPS Drop -> KEDA (RPS/Queue) -> Pause Pods (-10) -> API Pods (10->100)); Leading Metric Trigger & Pause-Pod Preemption (STEADY (10 pods) -> KEDA SURGE (<15s) -> PREEMPT (<1s)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Lowering the CPU HPA target from `70%` to `30%` wastes `2.3x` steady-state compute and **still** suffers `90–110 s` EC2 node provisioning delays when a 10x surge arrives, because new pods sit in `Pending` state. Detect surges in `< 15 s` and bring warm capacity online in `< 20 s`: **Leading Metrics via KEDA / Prometheus Adapter**: Scale on `envoy_http_rq_rate` / in-flight requests per pod.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Leading-metric autoscaling + warm node buffers are essential for flash-traffic workloads: **Ticketing & Flash-Sale Drops**: Scales out ahead of queue saturation during scheduled on-sales.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: KEDA Leading Metrics, Pause-Pod Buffer, and Surge Policies

explanation.foundation: Detect surges in `< 15 s` and bring warm capacity online in `< 20 s`:
explanation.core:
- **Leading Metrics via KEDA / Prometheus Adapter**: Scale on `envoy_http_rq_rate` / in-flight requests per pod (15s scrape) instead of lagging CPU utilization, with aggressive `behavior.scaleUp` (`100%` or `+30 pods / 15s`, `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0`).
- **Over-Provisioning Pause Pods (`PriorityClass: -10`)**: Run a `15%` warm buffer of zero-CPU-work `pause` pods on pre-provisioned EC2 nodes; when real API pods scale up, Kubernetes preempts pause pods in `< 1 s` (zero 110s node boot wait!).
- **Fast Image Pull + Readiness + Edge Shedding**: Pre-pull images (`DaemonSet`), use AppCDS/CRaC or GraalVM to cut JVM startup from `35 s` to `< 10 s`, and apply Envoy load shedding on existing 10 pods during the brief handoff.
